author: Athul Prem

full_channel_comparison.method: The five signed, unit-power incident, reflected and transmitted modes are aligned by section mass overlap. Gates apply to absolute changes in summed T or R per drive and to absolute complex coefficient changes. Per-entry power fractions use squared coefficient magnitudes. Phases refer to the original end planes.
full_channel_comparison.scope: All four comparisons change both the central footprint resolution and the solve platform. They quantify finite changes across the saved configurations at the two endpoint frequencies.

observable: D = C(995 MHz) - C(1000 MHz), with C(f) = 100 [R_100nm(f) - R_200nm(f)] in percentage points.
exploratory_target_basis: Ten percent of the absolute D on the prior independently remeshed 225 nm control.
resource_projection_scope: The Windows private-memory projection scales previous Windows direct-solve peaks by stiffness nonzero count. Windows response receipts report private commit. Lawrence receipts give their Slurm memory allocation, sampled process-tree resident set size and kernel-reported peak child resident set size. Factor fill and available system resources can vary on another run.
scope: T and R are fractions of each native incident drive's power at the original end planes. Matches use the +x incident fields and reciprocal mass-weighted overlaps at fixed y and normalized thickness. They support correspondence at the two sampled frequencies. The observed D increment measures finite response sensitivity. Continuum error, continuous branch identity, all-channel complex convergence, through-thickness and hole-wall uncertainty, and frequency convergence remain unresolved.
